messages:
noelle: Quick thread - support saw a few requests billed to the wrong org. Suspect header bleed on reused connections. Minimal repro below.

noelle: repro:
```bash
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer projless_foo\" -H \"X-Request-ID: r-foo-1\" -H \"X-Org: old-tenant\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hey\"}'
```
Edge response includes `X-Org: old-tenant` but auth metadata owner=new-tenant. Console shows count under old-tenant.

harry: This matches the keep-alive affinity issue. Our fast-path sometimes skips header enrichment after auth. We should prevent client headers from leaking through.

kevin: Options: (1) always overwrite X-Org post-auth (safe, small perf hit); (2) auth-service emits `X-Auth-Owner` signed by HMAC and edge trusts that (faster). I prefer 2 but need spoof-proofing.

noelle: Agree on 2. Plan: auth-service resolves owner for projectless keys -> set `X-Internal-Auth-Owner: <org>` with HMAC sig header `X-Auth-Signature`. Edge strips client-provided org headers, validates signature, and sets `X-Telemetry-Owner` when feature flag `prefer_internal_owner` is on.

mary: Telemetry/console: while canary is on we should emit `attribution_conflict_count` and sample up to N mismatches to S3 with request_id and both owners. Console request detail should surface both values if they differ.

harry: Security: strip any incoming internal headers before enrichment. HMAC key rotation must be supported; log verification failures. If signature invalid, edge should fall back to previous behavior and increment `auth_signature_failures`.

kevin: Rollout: `prefer_internal_owner` default off. Canary 5% internal for 6h -> monitor `attribution_conflict_count`, `quota_delta_by_org`, `auth_signature_failures`. If stable, expand to sandbox 30% for 24h, then global. Rollback by toggling flag.

ops-bot: deploy-scheduler: Canary window reserved 2026-04-10 02:00-05:00 UTC. Notifying oncall.

mary: I'll add console badge mock and the telemetry panels. QA please add spoofing test to ensure HMAC validation blocks client header injection.

kevin: I'll open auth PR for header + HMAC. Harry will own edge changes and flag. Noelle will coordinate rollout doc.

noelle: Thanks — will ping support and docs once PRs are up. :thumbsup:
